page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1ne.8xlarge is a storage-dense big data server configuration built on the KVM hypervisor. Compute is provided by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 32 dedicated vCPUs matched with 128 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 allocation ratio of 4 GB of system memory per vCPU. It does not include hardware GPU acceleration.

A primary technical characteristic of this instance is its massive bundled local storage array, offering 94,489 GB of local hard disk drive (HDD) capacity. For distributed communication and high-volume data ingestion, the instance includes a baseline network throughput of 20 Gbps. It does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring dedicated VPC networking setups for external access.

Because the storage profile is based on mechanical HDDs rather than solid-state NVMe media, the instance prioritizes massive sequential throughput and terabyte-per-dollar raw capacity density over random I/O latency. Workload fit includes distributed processing clusters, Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) data nodes, Apache Kafka streaming clusters, large log analytics backends, and sequential batch ETL pipelines requiring immense local storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1ne.8xlarge is a big data cloud instance designed for high-density local storage and distributed processing. Powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor with x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs and 128 GB of memory, maintaining a 4 GB per vCPU allocation. The defining hardware feature is an integrated 94,489 GB local HDD storage capacity alongside a 20 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance contains no GPU acceleration and does not come with complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The pairing of extensive mechanical storage capacity and multi-core processing makes this server a practical fit for cost-effective mass storage environments. It is structured for data-intensive processing architectures including Hadoop HDFS storage nodes, Apache Kafka pipelines, centralized log archiving, and large-scale sequential batch ETL processing.
